name: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS)
eligibility: Current high school sophomore or junior. Must be at least 16 years old by program start.
aid: Need-based financial aid available covering up to 100% of program fee. ~35-40% of participants receive aid. Need-aware for international applicants.
notes: Highly selective. Early Action has slightly higher acceptance rate. $6,500 covers tuition, housing, meals, materials. Travel not included. CT-based but draws global applicants.

name: Jackson Laboratory High School Summer Student Program (Farmington, CT)
eligibility: Current high school juniors and seniors (rising juniors/seniors). Must be 16+ by program start. U.S. citizenship or permanent residency generally required. Strong science background (AP Biology, AP Chemistry recommended).
aid: Paid program — $3,500 stipend for 6 weeks.
notes: Prestigious biomedical research program. Applications open December, close late January. Program runs ~mid-June through late July. Highly competitive for high school students.

name: UConn PNB Summer High School Research Program
eligibility: High school students, typically rising juniors and seniors. Must be 16+ by program start. Connecticut residency preferred.
aid: Paid — stipend of approximately $2,000-$3,000 for 6 weeks (~30-35 hrs/week).
notes: UConn Department of Physiology & Neurobiology. Strong hands-on lab experience. No cost; paid stipend. Good for students interested in neuroscience/pre-med.

name: UConn InSPIRE High School Research Internship
eligibility: High school juniors and seniors (ages 16+). Strong STEM academic record. Requires resume, transcript, personal statement, and science teacher recommendation.
aid: Paid internship — stipend provided.
notes: Located at UConn Health in Farmington, CT. Research areas: infectious disease, microbiology, immunology. Competitive admissions.

name: UConn MentorConnect High School Research Program
eligibility: High school students, typically rising juniors and seniors. Must be 16+ for most positions. CT residency preferred.
aid: Program is free; some positions may offer stipends (varies by mentor/department).
notes: Broad research areas beyond STEM. Best approach: create profile in fall, reach out to faculty directly. Applications open in winter, matching through spring.

name: Yale Pathways to Science Summer Program
eligibility: Current high school students in grades 9-12. Must be at least 14 by program start. No GPA minimum, but must demonstrate strong STEM interest.
aid: Completely free — includes tuition, housing, meals, and all activities. Students cover transportation to/from Yale only.
notes: Accessible entry to Yale STEM. Requires teacher recommendation, transcript, personal statement (~500 words). Competitive but lower barrier than YYGS. CT-based students have no travel cost.

name: UConn ECE Summer High School Research Internship
eligibility: Rising 11th and 12th grade high school students. Interest in engineering, IoT, and biosensors.
aid: Paid — stipend of $500-$700 for the 2-week session.
notes: Short commitment (2 weeks) but focused, hands-on prototyping. UConn Storrs campus. Good for exploring engineering before committing to longer programs.

name: Connecticut Science & Engineering Fair (CSEF)
eligibility: CT residents or students enrolled in CT schools (grades 7-12). Fishers Island, NY students also eligible.
aid: No cost to participate. Prizes and scholarships awarded to winners. ISEF advancement unlocks additional awards and prestige.
notes: ISEF affiliation adds significant college app value. Start project research in summer/early fall. 2026 fair was March 8 at Quinnipiac University. Check for 2027 dates from late 2026.

name: UConn Health Summer High School Research Internship
eligibility: Connecticut residents, rising juniors and seniors. Must be 16+ by program start.
aid: Paid program — stipend provided.
notes: UConn Health's main high school research pathway. Biomedical/clinical focus. Farmington campus. Requires transcript and recommendations.

name: PSAT/NMSQT 2025
eligibility: 11th grade (rising 12th) or 10th grade (rising 11th) can also take it
aid: Fee waivers available for qualifying low-income students
notes: Test date: October 2025 (primary Wednesday + Saturday alternate, exact dates TBA by school). Registration handled entirely by your high school — contact the guidance counselor. Fee capped at $18 by College Board. School coordinates its own internal registration deadline (likely late Aug/early Sep 2025). Also qualifies students for National Merit Scholarship Program. Registration: https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/psat-nmsqt; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: SAT — August 2026
eligibility: All students
aid: Fee waivers available for eligible low-income 11th/12th graders covering full cost plus free score sends
notes: Test date: August 22, 2026. Late registration deadline: August 11, 2026 ($38 late fee). Digital format. Registration: https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat/dates-deadlines

name: ACT — September 2026 (projected)
eligibility: All students
aid: Fee waivers available for eligible low-income students (up to 4 free tests)
notes: Projected test date: September 12, 2026. Late registration (projected): August 28, 2026 (+$39 late fee). ACT with Writing costs $97. Official schedule expected spring 2026. Registration: https://www.act.org/content/act/en/products-and-services/the-act/registration.html

name: CLT — February 2026
eligibility: 11th/12th graders (and adults)
aid: Fee waivers available for eligible low-income students; one free retake for all testers
notes: Test date: February 14, 2026. Register at cltexam.com/register. CLT10 ($50) and CLT8 ($45) also available. Accepted by ~250+ colleges including many Christian/classical schools and a growing number of mainstream universities. Registration: https://www.cltexam.com/register/; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: Junior Olympics 2027
eligibility: U.S. Fencing competitive membership required. Born 2007-2011 for Cadet; born 2005-2009 for Junior. Must qualify through regional points or at-large application.
aid: False
notes: Registration typically opens Oct-Nov 2026. Early reg ~$150/event, late ~$225. Considered the most prestigious youth national championship.

name: Summer Nationals 2026 & July Challenge
eligibility: Valid USA Fencing competitive membership. Qualification required for Division I and some youth events; Division II/III open to all with membership and appropriate rating.
aid: False
notes: Early reg ~$140-170/event, standard ~$200-230/event. Late reg ~$260-310/event. Portland is a travel destination. Register early for best rates.

name: February NAC 2026 - Cincinnati
eligibility: Valid USA Fencing competitive membership. Open to all fencers with age-appropriate and classification-appropriate events.
aid: False
notes: Regular reg $150/event (deadline Jan 28), late $225/event (deadline Jan 31). Admin fee ~$5.25. FIE 1600N mask required for senior events.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: March NAC 2026 - Cleveland
eligibility: Valid USA Fencing membership. Y14 for ages 14 and under; Division II for fencers with C rating or below.
aid: False
notes: Closest NAC to CT. Driving distance from Connecticut (~7 hours). Estimated cost $75-100 per event (early reg).; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: April NAC / Division I & Parafencing Nationals 2026 - Richmond
eligibility: Division I requires national points or qualifying result. Junior (U20) is open entry with USA Fencing membership.
aid: False
notes: Closer to CT than West Coast events. Junior event is open entry. Division I requires qualification but Junior is the main draw for rising 11th graders.; deadline may have passed

name: U.S. Fencing Center College Prep Recruiting Camp
eligibility: High school fencers entering grades 9-12 in Fall 2026. 2025 graduates also eligible.
aid: False
notes: $525 includes instruction, college seminar, individual recruiting video, and T-shirt. Camp runs 10am-3pm daily. San Antonio location (flight required from CT).

name: Columbia University Fencing National Team Camp 2026
eligibility: Competitive fencers, typically ages 13-18 with tournament experience. National Team Camp tier for advanced fencers.
aid: False
notes: Commuter $875, Overnight $1,295 (2025 pricing; 2026 TBD). National Team Camp $1,000 commuter / $1,450 overnight. $30 late fee after May 1. $100 deposit required. One of the top college camps accessible from CT.

name: Candlewood Fencing Center Pre-Nats Competitive Foil Camp
eligibility: Fencers of all experience levels, split by weapon and experience. Competitive foil track available.
aid: False
notes: $550 for Pre-Nats Foil Camp. $600 for regular Norwalk Foil Camp. Local to CT - no travel costs. Private lesson add-ons available for $50.

name: Vassar College Prep Fencing Camp 2026
eligibility: High school fencers grades 9-12 interested in college fencing.
aid: False
notes: 2025 pricing: ~$875-950. Overnight camp at Vassar's campus. Focus on recruiting strategy and college preparation alongside fencing training.

name: NYAC Fencing College Prep Camp 2026
eligibility: High school fencers preparing for college recruiting.
aid: False
notes: 2025 camp was $600-800 range for week. 2026 dates TBD (likely June). One of the most prestigious fencing clubs in the U.S. Travel from CT via train is simple.

name: National Merit Scholarship Program
eligibility: U.S. high school juniors (class of 2028); U.S. citizen or permanent resident; must take PSAT/NMSQT in fall of junior year
aid: Up to $2,500 one-time national scholarships; corporate and college-sponsored awards vary
notes: Entry is through the PSAT/NMSQT, administered by College Board. Semifinalists (~16,000) announced September 2027. ~15,000 Finalists. ~7,500 winners. The PSAT is typically taken mid-October.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS)
eligibility: U.S. high school seniors (class of 2028) and U.S. citizens abroad; must submit original independent research
aid: Top 300: $2,000 (+ $2,000 to school). Top 40 Finalists: min $25,000 + all-expenses trip to DC. Top 10: $40,000-$250,000. Total >$1.8M.
notes: Application opens June 1, 2027. Deadline typically mid-November. Requires: research report, transcript, test scores (optional), essays, recommendations, activities list. Top 300 announced Jan 2028; Top 40 Jan 2028; Finals Week in DC March 2028.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
eligibility: Must be 18 or younger as of deadline; U.S. citizen or permanent resident residing in U.S., or on active U.S. military duty overseas
notes: Application opens Fall 2026. Two nominator forms required plus category-specific attachments. Winners must attend in-person/virtual awards ceremony in DC. Two-person teams allowed. 'Outside the Box' category for interdisciplinary work.

name: U.S. Presidential Scholars Program
eligibility: U.S. citizen or permanent resident; high school senior graduating Jan-Aug 2028; must take SAT or ACT on or before October 2027
aid: Presidential Scholar medallion and recognition; no cash award but carries significant distinction for college admissions
notes: Application opens August 2027. Testing deadline: SAT/ACT must be taken by Oct 2027 (end of junior year). General component students are initially identified via SAT/ACT scores — no initial application needed. CTE requires state nomination. Arts requires YoungArts participation. 1 boy + 1 girl per state + at-large.

name: U.S. Senate Youth Program (USSYP)
eligibility: High school junior or senior (class of 2028 or 2029) serving in an elected or appointed student government position for the 2027-2028 school year
aid: $10,000 undergraduate college scholarship (for each of 104 delegates); all-expenses-paid trip to Washington, D.C.
notes: Application process managed by state Departments of Education. Deadline varies by state (typically Sep-Nov 2027). 63rd Annual Program: Washington Week March 2028. Extremely competitive — 2 per state. 62nd program (2026-27) held March 6-9, 2027.

name: Prudential Spirit of Community Awards
eligibility: U.S. students grades 5-12 (rising 11th grader eligible) who have engaged in volunteer service
aid: State Honorees: $1,000 + engraved silver medallion + expense-paid trip to DC. National Honorees: additional $5,000 + gold medallion + crystal trophy for school/nonprofit
notes: Application opens August 2027, deadline early November 2027. 75 State Honorees (middle + high school per state + DC). 10 National Honorees. Running since 1995. Program is a competitive national award, distinct from the hour-based President's Volunteer Service Award.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
eligibility: Grades 9-12 (rising 11th grader eligible); must first compete in and win an ISEF-affiliated regional/state science fair
cost: Varies by affiliated fair (typically $0-$50 for fair registration)
aid: Top award: $75,000. Over $8M total annually. Multiple category awards, special awards, and scholarships from partner organizations.
notes: ISEF 2027 projected for May 2027 (likely 2nd-3rd week). 22 STEM categories. ~1,800 finalists from ~75 countries. Rising 11th grader should start research project summer 2026 and identify local affiliated fair by Fall 2026. ISEF 2026 in Columbus, OH (May 10-15, 2026).

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
eligibility: High school students grades 9-12 (rising 11th grader eligible); U.S. citizen or permanent resident
aid: National scholarships up to $12,000; regional awards vary. All-expenses-paid national symposium for regional winners.
notes: Regional deadlines vary (typically Oct-Jan). Rising 11th grader should start research project summer 2026-2027. Administered by National Youth Science Foundation. 5 regional symposia covering the U.S. Winners advance to National JSHS. Website currently being updated for 2027-2028 cycle.

name: Yale Young Global Scholars — Law & Politics (LPC)
eligibility: Grade 10-11, age 16-18 by program start
aid: Need-based financial aid available (applied within main application)
notes: 3 sessions offered Jun-Jul 2026 (similar to 2025 structure). $6,500 tuition + ~$95 application fee. Highly selective. Sessions: ~Jun 22-Jul 4, Jul 6-18, Jul 20-Aug 1. Early Action recommended.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: National High School Mock Trial Championship (NHSMTC)
eligibility: High school students on a team that wins its state mock trial championship
aid: Varies by state; some state bar associations offer travel grants
notes: CT state finals held at CT Supreme Court. Civics First (civicsfirstct.org) runs CT high school mock trial. Staples, Hall, Wilton, Greenwich are top CT programs. 2025 nationals were in Hartford CT; 2026 location TBD.; deadline may have passed

name: Empire Mock Trial National Championship
eligibility: High school mock trial teams (grades 9-12)
aid: Need-based scholarships available for qualifying teams
notes: April 17-19, 2026 in Los Angeles, CA. $1,500-$2,500 estimated team fee plus travel/lodging. Competitive invitation/application process. Registration opens fall 2025.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: National Mock Trial Invitational (NMTI) — Chicago
eligibility: High school mock trial teams by invitation/application
aid: None specified
notes: Feb 6-8, 2026 in Chicago. $375/team registration + mandatory hotel block (min 5 rooms, 3 nights). Roster cap: 15 students. Run by Intraspect Legal Foundation.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: Princeton Model Congress (PMC)
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12)
aid: Need-based aid may be available; contact organizers
notes: Feb 15-18, 2026 at Washington Hilton, Washington DC. $185/student registration fee (covers materials, committees, events). Travel/lodging/meals not included. Session topics include congressional debate, Supreme Court simulation.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: Harvard Model Congress (HMC) — Boston
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12)
aid: Some scholarships available; check website
notes: Late Feb / early Mar 2026 in Boston, MA. ~$200-$300 delegate registration. Hotel packages offered separately. Also has San Francisco, Asia, Middle East, and Europe conferences.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: National High School Moot Court Competition (AMCA)
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12), teams of 2
aid: Some regional hosts offer fee waivers
notes: Registration opens Aug-Sep. Regional qualifiers Jan-Feb 2026. National Championship Mar-Apr 2026. $150-$300 team fee. Case problem released Sep-Oct. Teams argue both Petitioner and Respondent sides.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: We the People: The Citizen and the Constitution — National Finals
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12) on a team that wins state competition
aid: Many schools fundraise; state bar associations and grants available
notes: National Finals Apr 24-28, 2026 at Gaylord National Resort, National Harbor MD. $875/team registration. Total team cost $20k-30k including travel/lodging for 20-25 students. 6 units covering constitutional themes.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: Telluride Association Summer Program (TASP)
eligibility: High school juniors (rising seniors), any country
aid: Fully funded — tuition, room, board, books, field trips, and travel all covered
notes: ~3-5% acceptance rate. Application opens Nov 2025. 6 weeks late Jun-early Aug. U.S. and international students eligible. No GPA requirement — looks for intellectual curiosity. Seminars often at Cornell or University of Michigan. Eligible for 2027 summer only.; repeats annually, check for 2027 dates

name: YMCA Youth Conference on National Affairs (CONA)
eligibility: High school students who qualify through state YMCA Youth & Government program
aid: Need-based scholarships may be available through local YMCA
notes: Jun 28-Jul 3, 2026 at Blue Ridge Assembly, Black Mountain, NC. ~$1,120 plus travel. State-level YIG programs run Sep-Apr. Bill proposals, committee hearings, leadership development. CT YMCA Youth & Government contact needed.; deadline may have passed

name: Close Up Foundation — Washington DC High School Program
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12)
aid: Need-based financial aid up to 50% of tuition; fundraising support available
notes: 4-day, 5-day, and 7-day program options. $2,295 standard 5-day program (2025 pricing; 2026 similar or ~3-5% higher). Includes lodging, meals, program materials, insurance. Registration opens fall 2025. NextGen Roundtable: Decision 2026 also available.

name: APIA Scholarship
eligibility: AAPI heritage, high school senior enrolling as degree-seeking undergraduate at U.S. accredited college/university, U.S. citizen/permanent resident.
notes: Indian American students are eligible as Asian American. Even though need is prioritized, merit and heritage are factors. Strong option given South Asian heritage alignment.

name: Vincent Chin Scholarship (AALDEF)
eligibility: Asian American high school senior residing in Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Jersey, or New York. Pursuing higher education.
notes: Directly available to CT residents. Named after Vincent Chin, civil rights icon. Emphasizes Asian American identity and community engagement in essays.

name: OCA-UPS Gold Mountain Scholarship
eligibility: Asian Pacific American (APA) high school senior, first-generation college student (neither parent completed a 4-year degree), U.S. citizen/permanent resident.
notes: Good fit only if student is first-generation college attendee. Heritage-aligned for Indian American students. Typically opens December-February cycle.

name: Hindu American Foundation Dharma Digest Scholarship
eligibility: High school senior planning to attend college in the fall. Must submit essay on Hindu philosophy prompt.
notes: Strong cultural fit for Indian American Hindu student. Essay-based competition. Deadline typically February. Only one winner per cycle, so competitive but niche audience reduces applicant pool.

name: Prudential Emerging Visionaries
eligibility: Ages 14-18, U.S. citizen/permanent resident, leading a project or initiative addressing a financial or societal challenge.
aid: $1,000 to $15,000 plus mentorship and summit
notes: Leadership and community impact focused. Good fit for student with a community service or social entrepreneurship project. No income or ethnicity restrictions.

name: Elks National Foundation Most Valuable Student Scholarship
eligibility: Current high school senior, U.S. citizen, planning to enroll in a four-year U.S. college/university. Judged on scholarship, leadership, and financial need.
aid: $4,000 to $30,000 over four years
notes: Large awards pool (500 winners). Financial need is a factor but not exclusive. High-income family may be at disadvantage on need criterion. Still worth applying given 500 award slots.

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO) 2027
eligibility: High school students grades 9-12 enrolled in a US school
aid: merit
notes: Excellent fit for a biology-interested student. Open Exam is free and administered at school. Should ask biology teacher in Fall 2026 to register as USABO test center. Prepare using Campbell Biology and USABO practice exams. High competitiveness but very achievable with dedicated study. Top 20 make National Finals (all expenses paid).

name: Regeneron International Science & Engineering Fair (ISEF) 2027
eligibility: Grades 9-12, no older than 20; must qualify through an SSP-affiliated fair
aid: merit
notes: Ultimate goal for science fair pipeline. Path: CSEF Jan registration -> CSEF March -> ISEF May. Extremely competitive but very strong signal for college admissions. Start research project ASAP. Consider university mentorship for higher-quality projects. Biology categories include Cellular/Molecular Bio, Microbiology, Biochemistry, Plant Sciences, Animal Sciences.

name: AMC 12 A/B 2026
eligibility: High school students in grade 12 or below; must take at a registered school site
aid: none
notes: Strong alignment given student's STEM profile. Register through school in September 2026. Aim for AIME qualification (top ~5%). This is a junior-year opportunity. Consider taking AMC 10 as practice sophomore year if available. Indian American students often perform very well; no ethnic bias concern. Competitiveness for AIME is high but achievable with AoPS preparation.

name: AIME (American Invitational Mathematics Examination) 2027
eligibility: Invitation only: top ~2.5% AMC 10 scorers or top ~5% AMC 12 scorers
aid: none
notes: This is the follow-on to AMC 12. Not a standalone opportunity — student must first do well on AMC 12. AIME qualification alone is a strong college admissions signal for STEM. AIME score of 7+ is competitive for selective programs. For biology interest, strong math foundation is complementary.

name: Science Olympiad National Tournament 2027
eligibility: High school students (Div C, grades 9-12); membership is school-based, ~$250-300 per school team
aid: none
notes: Excellent team-based competition. Biology events include Anatomy & Physiology, Cell Biology, Disease Detectives, Ecology. Good for building broad science knowledge. Requires school team formation — check with teachers. Not as individually prestigious as USABO/ISEF but great for depth and team collaboration experience.

name: BioGENEius Challenge 2027
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12
aid: merit
notes: Terrific fit for biology interest with biotech focus. Can use same research project as science fair. Lower volume of applicants than ISEF, so potentially higher visibility. Strong signal for pre-med/biotech career interest.

name: MIT THINK Scholars Program 2027
eligibility: High school students in the US
aid: merit
notes: Less competitive than RSI but still prestigious. Good for testing a research idea with lower stakes. Funding of $1,000 helps cover project costs. Application is a proposal, not completed research — so student can apply with a summer 2027 research plan.

name: Genes in Space 2027
eligibility: US students in grades 7-12, including US territories and DoD schools worldwide
aid: merit
notes: Unique opportunity combining biology and space. Less competitive than ISEF/USABO but very distinctive for college apps. The 'my experiment went to space' angle is memorable. Good supplemental activity alongside main research project.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI) at MIT
eligibility: Current high school juniors (rising seniors); U.S. citizens and international students
aid: Full scholarship — travel, room, board, and all program costs covered
notes: Most selective summer research program in the US. Runs late June through early August. Biology research available. Student must be a current junior (Class of 2027 in the 2026-27 school year). For summer 2027, applications open Nov 2026, deadline ~Dec 2026.

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
eligibility: Current high school juniors (rising seniors); also bright sophomores considered; open to U.S. and international students
aid: Full need-based financial aid available including travel scholarships; no income cutoff
notes: Biochemistry track involves protein-ligand molecular docking for drug discovery. No grades or credits — pure research experience. Applications open December 2026.

name: Simons Summer Research Program
eligibility: Rising seniors (current juniors); U.S. citizens or permanent residents
aid: Fully funded — stipend provided to participants
notes: Runs approximately June 29 - August 7 (based on 2026 dates). Applications typically open November/December, deadline February. Biology research available through multiple STEM departments.

name: Anson L. Clark Scholars Program
eligibility: High school juniors and seniors; must be at least 17 by program start; unweighted GPA 3.5+
aid: Fully funded — room, board, meals covered; $750 tax-free stipend; travel support up to $500
notes: Applications open January, deadline mid-February. Runs approximately June 16 - August 1. Student must turn 17 before program start date.

name: NIH High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP)
eligibility: Must be at least 16; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; currently enrolled in high school
aid: Paid — monthly stipend ~$2,000-$2,400 for high school students
notes: Applications open November 2026, deadline February/March 2027. Highly competitive. Students work in NIH intramural research labs alongside professional scientists. CT-based student would need to arrange housing near NIH campus.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
eligibility: Current juniors or seniors (Classes of 2027 or 2028); must be 16+; U.S. citizen or permanent resident
aid: Free — minimum $500 stipend; up to $2,500 for students with financial need
notes: Runs approximately June 8 - July 30. No housing provided — student must arrange own housing near Stanford if not local. Strong biology/medicine focus. Applications open December 2026.

name: UChicago Research in the Biological Sciences (RIBS)
eligibility: Rising juniors and seniors; must have completed at least one year of high school biology; grades 10-12
aid: Need-based financial aid available
notes: Excellent for deep biology focus. Students present original research at closing symposium. Applications open November 2026, priority deadline early February 2027.

name: Georgetown Law High School Academy
eligibility: Rising sophomores, juniors, and seniors (grades 10-12)
aid: Limited need-based aid available
notes: Good match for law interest. Based on ~$1,200-$1,500/week residential pricing. Located in Washington DC — can complement biology interest through bioethics/health law exposure. Multiple sessions June through July.

name: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes
eligibility: Grades 8-11; some courses have prerequisites
aid: Need-based financial aid available
notes: Unique option for biology+law — student could take one biology course and one law course in separate sessions. Applications open December 2026, priority deadline early 2027.

name: Harvard Pre-College Program
eligibility: Rising sophomores, juniors, and seniors; ages 16-19
aid: Need-based financial aid available
notes: Student could attend one session. May combine with other summer commitments. Non-graded, focus on exploration. Applications typically open December 2026.

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
eligibility: Grades 7-12
aid: Fee waivers available for students with financial need via online portal
notes: Most competitive national writing program for teens. $10/entry. Regional deadlines vary mid-December. National Board accepting submissions for 2026-2027 cycle. National ceremonies at Carnegie Hall in June. Also pathway to National Student Poets Program (grades 10-11, $5,000 scholarship).

name: John Locke Institute Essay Competition
eligibility: Under 19 years old as of submission deadline; Junior Prize for under 15; Senior Prize for ages 15-18
aid: Free entry. Late registration $10 USD; late submission extensions available for £25-75 GBP. Travel grants may be awarded.
notes: One of the most prestigious international essay competitions. Free to enter if registered early. Registration opens ~February, submissions April-May. Academic conference and awards dinner at Oxford in October. AI tools permitted but may negatively affect assessment. One academic referee required. Junior and Senior entries judged separately.

name: National History Day
eligibility: Grades 6-12
aid: Many regional affiliates provide fee support or waivers; no national entry fee
notes: Paper category judged digitally (no on-site presentation). Must use annotated bibliography (primary/secondary sources). Process paper required. Plagiarism detection used. AI-generated text prohibited. School contests typically Feb-Mar, regionals Mar-Apr, state Apr-May, national June. Paper entries do not require on-site attendance at nationals but students attend awards. National contest typically draws ~3,000 participants.

name: YoungArts National Arts Competition (Writing)
eligibility: Grades 10-12 or ages 15-18 as of December 1 of application year; US citizens, permanent residents, or legally able to receive taxable income in US with SSN
aid: Free to apply; scholarships and cash awards
notes: Highly prestigious with strong college admissions recognition. Application opens ~June, closes ~October. Multiple writing subcategories allowed. Winners can receive up to $10,000. National YoungArts Week in Miami for top winners. Also connects to US Presidential Scholars in the Arts program.

name: Bennington College Young Writers Awards
eligibility: Grades 9-12 worldwide
aid: Free entry. No application fee.
notes: 1st, 2nd, 3rd place winners per category plus Distinguished submissions recognized by grade level. All winners receive cash prizes and scholarships. Grade 12 students must complete Bennington Common/Coalition App first. Grade 9-11 submit directly via entry link. One category only per student.

name: The Ayn Rand Institute Essay Contests - Anthem
eligibility: Grades 8-12 worldwide, ages 13+. Must be enrolled in school during contest period.
aid: Free entry
notes: Also eligible for Fountainhead contest (deadline April 28, 2027, 1st prize $10,000, grades 11-12) and Atlas Shrugged contest (deadline October 28, 2027, 1st prize $20,000, grades 11-12). Can submit one essay per author per contest period. 800-1,600 words for Fountainhead/Atlas Shrugged. Established program with substantial scholarship prizes.

name: Princeton University 10-Minute Play Contest
eligibility: Current 11th grade high school students only
aid: Free entry. Winner receives full scholarship to Princeton Summer Theater Program.
notes: Very selective (single winner). Not explicitly limited to NJ/tri-state area per most listings. Requires cover page with name, DOB, school, address, phone, email. Prize is full scholarship to 6-week summer theater program + play production. Submit online via Lewis Center for the Arts. Check arts.princeton.edu in fall for exact deadline.

name: Foyle Young Poets of the Year Award
eligibility: Ages 11-17 as of July 31 of competition year; open internationally
aid: Free entry
notes: One of the largest youth poetry competitions globally. 85 winners per year. Publication in prestigious anthology. Top 15 winners receive mentoring and a commendation. Previous winners have gone on to major literary careers. Deadline is always July 31 annually. Winners announced in the fall.

name: JASNA Jane Austen Essay Contest
eligibility: Grades 9-12 (High School division); also College and Graduate divisions
aid: Free entry. No JASNA membership required. Prize includes free lodging at AGM.
notes: High School division requires characters from one novel or two or more books. College/graduate divisions require at least two novels. 2026 topic: 'Men and Boys in Jane Austen's Novels' (deadline June 1, 2026). 2027 topic announced ~early 2026/2027. Late entries accepted until next morning. No membership required.

name: Ocean Awareness Contest

aid: Free entry
